680	Apparently, and this is what creates the stimulus for his inner movement, to do something that is
681	above reason and knowledge.
682	That is what makes him a tzaddik; it is not only a matter of influence.
683	How much he influences someone else, what he is capable of.
684	The very fact that he makes this movement, which is above reason and knowledge, will certainly also influence others, but
685	the movement is first of all in him, in his inner point.
686	Certainly.
687	"Influencer," when we say it, does not mean it in the external sense, like social-media influencers
688	or all kinds of that sort.
689	An influencer is not someone who influences another to do what he wants.
690	An influencer is on the way to being a tzaddik.
691	That is called a tzaddik; one who bestows is called a tzaddik.
692	One who bestows is a person who walks the path of bestowal toward others.
693	That is what is called a bestower.
694	He bestows good on others, he gives of himself.
695	That is called a bestowing person.
696	As if it is...
697	It could be that he will not be in that level, if he is in an environment that is very bad,
698	hostile, even criminal, and he makes there some very great movement outward.
699	But he did, he did influence through the very movement, because he...
700	Suddenly, the fact that he makes a movement within himself will certainly also create
701	a movement in that environment.
702	They will not follow him, but it creates something, because it is a resonance that we created.
703	You are right.
704	They tell of Baal HaSulam that he sat in the beit midrash and learned Torah, and the whole war, I think
705	it was the war of '48, the War of Independence, the whole War of Independence
706	moved according to Baal HaSulam's Torah learning.
707	He described there what he was learning and directed that things would happen in this way and that way,
708	so we see from this example that a tzaddik sits and learns Torah and influences the whole world.
709	It does not have to be specifically through direct contact or contact of one kind or another. We also see that things are learned, for example, in our beit
710	midrash, that are spoken about in other places that had no direct connection
711	to us. They speak in our language. The concept of "together," which I think the Rav
712	has been speaking about for many years: see how it entered the people of Israel as a concept
713	of "together we will win," and the whole use of this concept "together," even a political party, it seems, is called
714	"Together." The concept of "together" took root relatively recently, as I see it,
715	and in the Sulam they have been speaking about it for many years. So the concepts that are spoken about, the Torah of the tzaddikim,
716	is a Torah that takes up volume and expands even without them being present in every
717	single place.
718	There are many things that could be discussed; we will stop here, but with the help of HaShem, in the next lesson in Machshevet HaLev we will continue
719	this article; we still have a few more questions to learn and to answer.
